# Configuration

<!-- Generated from crates/vtium-settings/src/keys.rs; do not edit. `VTIUM_BLESS=1 cargo test -p vtium generated_files` rewrites it. -->

vtium reads one file, `vtium.conf` in the configuration directory (`--configdir`, `/etc/vtium` by default), then its command line, which wins over the file. vtium never reads `/etc/kmscon` or a seat file such as `seat0.seat.conf`: a `kmscon.conf` from kmscon is copied to `/etc/vtium/vtium.conf` by hand, and vtium reads the keys `kmscon` takes, in the ways the vtium crate's README, "Reading the configuration", sets out. With no file, vtium runs its defaults and its compiled-in heads and rules. The file is read once, at start: a change applies when vtium starts again, as at a restart of its service.

The file has two parts. Every line above the first section heading is the top level: vtium's own keys, the defaults every head inherits, and the flow's `version` and `policy`. From the first section heading on come the sections: a `[look NAME]` for each look, which names a frit and its size, a `[head NAME]` for each head, and one `[rules]` list, which sends each display and each input device to a head. A file with a section needs `version = 1`. A head's section wins over its look's, and its look's over the top level, for the keys the table below says each may set. The page [The sections of vtium.conf](head-file.md) describes each section and its keys.

vtium reads vtium.conf only when root owns it, or, for a vtium that runs as another user, that user, and neither its group nor others can write it or a directory above it. It reads none of a file that fails, runs its compiled-in configuration, and says which path fails and the command that mends it, `chown root:root PATH` or `chmod go-w PATH`.

`vtium check-config [--no-devices] [FILE]` reads vtium.conf, or FILE in its place to check it before it is installed, both its parts in one run, as the start would, through the start's parser and evaluator. It applies nothing, exits 1 on any warning of the keys and on each error and warning of the sections, each named with its line, and on a file whose flow wires no complete route: a display present that its first matching rule sends to a head that a keyboard present reaches. With no display or no keyboard present, or with `--no-devices`, it judges the rules alone and says so. It notes on standard output what it does not count: the density points convert at, and of the sections each rule sending input to a head by `id` or `name` alone, where no udev daemon runs, each rule using a key that reads udev's database, each rule using `connector-path:`, which it cannot check against the displays present since it opens no card to read a connector's `PATH`, a head no rule names, every head isolated, each head whose `vt` names only VTs on which vtium is not enabled, at boot or as logind's autovt, with the command that enables vtium on one of them, and what the devices present find: each rule matching none of them, each device no rule places with what the policy gives it, no head that can be the active head having a display, under a closed policy no keyboard reaching any head, a head claiming pointers while every keyboard is claimed elsewhere, every keyboard ignored, and a head whose only keyboard is one device. It reads the devices from sysfs and udev's database, `/run/udev/data`, and the VTs vtium is enabled on from systemd's unit links under `/etc/systemd`, and opens nothing under `/dev`. With `--no-devices`, or on a machine not started with systemd, it says that it did not check the heads' VTs. A FILE that root does not own, or that others can write, is checked all the same, with a note, since installing it makes it root's.

A top-level line holds one key: `key=value`, or a switch's `key` to turn it on and `no-key` to turn it off. A section's line is `key = value`. `#` starts a comment at the start of a line or after a blank; a `#` inside a word, or one that opens a `#rrggbb` value, is part of the value, and `\#` after a blank is a literal `#`. Spaces and tabs around the key and the value are dropped. On the command line a key is `--key=VALUE` or `--key VALUE`, and a switch `--key` or `--no-key`.

vtium reports, once at start, a top-level key it does not know, however often it appears, and a value it cannot use: a number out of bounds, which it clamps, and a value it cannot read, which it ignores, keeping the value the sources before it gave. An error in a section never drops a top-level key. It drops the section or the rule that holds it, or every section when it leaves their structure untrustworthy, as [Invalid files](head-file.md#invalid-files) describes. It reads at most 65536 bytes of the file and 8192 of a line.

Four key bindings had other names before the maintainer renamed them to more accepted terms: `grab-paste` is `key-paste`, `grab-reboot` is `key-reboot`, `grab-power-off` is `key-power-off`, and `grab-suspend` is `key-suspend`. vtium still reads each old name as its new one and reports each line that uses it, so that you can rename it. Where a source sets both names, the new one wins.

`install/vtium.conf.example` in `crates/vtium` lists the same keys at their defaults, under the same sections, then the compiled-in looks, heads and rules. Source names the GitHub issue, the specification or the released program each key comes from.

## Fonts and text

The console's font and its size, who draws box-drawing and block characters, how blinking text looks, and which way text runs.

| Key | Option | Type | Default | Bound | Read by | Set in | What | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `font-name` | `--font-name=VALUE` | text | unset | 4095 bytes, no control character | vtium-font | top level, `[look NAME]`, command line | The console's font. The value is the name of a font set (a frit file, `NAME.vtfrit` in `/etc/vtium/fonts`). It can also be the name of a kbd console font, or with `font-engine = psf` the path of a PSF font; vtium then uses that one font. When unset, vtium uses the font from vconsole.conf. If there is none, or vtium cannot find the font, vtium uses its built-in font and logs why. | kmscon's `font-name` key; [the issue that loads the configured font set](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/126) |
| `font-frits` | `--font-frits=VALUE` | path | `/etc/vtium/fonts` | absolute, 4095 bytes, no control character | vtium | top level, command line | The directory that holds the font sets (the `NAME.vtfrit` files that `font-name` names). It must be an absolute path; vtium ignores a relative or empty one and logs why. The default is the directory vtium was built with. | [the issue that loads the configured font set](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/126); the maintainer's decision of 2026-11-01 |
| `font-paths` | `--font-paths=VALUE` | paths, separated by `:` | unset | each absolute, 4095 bytes in all, no control character | vtium | top level, command line | The folders where vtium looks, in order, for installed fonts that a font set's `font:` lines name. Separate the folders with `:`, as in `PATH`; each must be an absolute path. The list replaces the built-in list. vtium skips a folder that is not an absolute path, uses the rest, and logs why. The list can reorder or leave out the system's folders. When unset, vtium searches `/usr/share/fonts` and `/usr/local/share/fonts`. A user's own folder, such as `~/.local/share/fonts`, is searched only when the list names it, and the font helper cannot read it before someone logs in, because it then runs as `nobody`. | [the configuration flow issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/299) |
| `font-engine` | `--font-engine=VALUE` | one of `freetype`, `pango`, `psf`, `unifont`, `8x16` | unset | the choices | vtium-font | top level, `[look NAME]`, command line | Which kind of font to use. When unset, vtium tries each kind the build supports, in the order listed. | kmscon's `font-engine` key |
| `font-size` | `--font-size=VALUE` | number (pt) | 0 | 0 to 2048, clamped | vtium-font | top level, `[look NAME]`, command line | The font size in points (1/72 inch). The size in pixels is points × DPI ÷ 72, at the display's density (`display-dpi`). It overrides a font set's `cell=` line. 0 picks a size to suit each display. | kmscon's `font-size` key; vtium-font's `CELL_SIDE_MAX`; [the issue that renders glyphs in the font helper](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/145) |
| `cell` | none | character cell, `WIDTHxHEIGHT` in pixels | unset | each side 6 to 96, no leading zero | vtium | `[look NAME]` | The size of a look's character cell, written as in a font set's `cell=` line (WIDTHxHEIGHT). It overrides the `cell=` and `size=` lines of the look's font set, and the top-level `font-size`. A `font-size` other than 0 in the same look overrides `cell`. When unset, the font set's `cell=` decides. | [the configuration flow issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/299) |
| `font-hinting` | `--font-hinting=VALUE` | one of `light`, `full` | unset | the choices | vtium-font | top level, `[look NAME]`, command line | How outline fonts are fitted to the pixel grid (hinting). It overrides a font set's `hinting=` line. `light` fits each character vertically only. `full` fits a TrueType font both ways, and treats a CFF font as `light`. Bitmap fonts are not hinted. This key has no effect yet: each font set's `hinting=` line decides, and `light` is used where it has none. | [the configuration flow issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/299) |
| `font-line-spacing` | `--font-line-spacing=VALUE` | number (%) | unset | 0 to 100, clamped | vtium-font | top level, `[look NAME]`, command line | Extra space between lines of text. It overrides a font set's `line-spacing=` line. The value is a whole percentage of the text height, rounded to whole pixels and split above and below each line, so the console has fewer lines. When `font-size` overrides a font set's `cell=` size, the character cell grows by the spacing. When unset, the font set's `line-spacing=` decides, and 0 where it has none. Letters keep their size in the middle of the taller line, and line and block characters stretch to fill it. A font set's `fit=` lines choose this for each set of characters. | [the line spacing issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/277) |
| `glyph-source` | `--glyph-source=VALUE` | one of `font`, `sprites`, `auto` | unset | the choices | vtium-font | top level, command line | Who draws box-drawing, block and similar characters (six ranges): the font, or vtium itself. `font` uses the font's characters, `sprites` uses vtium's own drawings, and `auto` uses the font's where the font has the character. When unset, vtium uses the font for each range the font covers completely and its own drawings for the rest; with the built-in unifont, vtium always draws them itself. | [the glyph source issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/85) |
| `glyph-source-box` | `--glyph-source-box=VALUE` | one of `font`, `sprites`, `auto` | unset | the choices | vtium-font | top level, command line | Overrides `glyph-source` for box drawing (U+2500 to U+257F). | [the glyph source issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/85) |
| `glyph-source-block` | `--glyph-source-block=VALUE` | one of `font`, `sprites`, `auto` | unset | the choices | vtium-font | top level, command line | Overrides `glyph-source` for block elements (U+2580 to U+259F). | [the glyph source issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/85) |
| `glyph-source-braille` | `--glyph-source-braille=VALUE` | one of `font`, `sprites`, `auto` | unset | the choices | vtium-font | top level, command line | Overrides `glyph-source` for Braille (U+2800 to U+28FF). | [the glyph source issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/85) |
| `glyph-source-sextants` | `--glyph-source-sextants=VALUE` | one of `font`, `sprites`, `auto` | unset | the choices | vtium-font | top level, command line | Overrides `glyph-source` for sextants (U+1FB00 to U+1FB3B). | [the glyph source issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/85) |
| `glyph-source-octants` | `--glyph-source-octants=VALUE` | one of `font`, `sprites`, `auto` | unset | the choices | vtium-font | top level, command line | Overrides `glyph-source` for octants (U+1CD00 to U+1CDE5). | [the glyph source issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/85) |
| `glyph-source-legacy` | `--glyph-source-legacy=VALUE` | one of `font`, `sprites`, `auto` | unset | the choices | vtium-font | top level, command line | Overrides `glyph-source` for the other block shapes of Symbols for Legacy Computing. | [the glyph source issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/85) |
| `missing` | `--missing=VALUE` | one of `box`, `hex` | `box` | the choices | vtium-font | top level, command line | What vtium shows for a character the font cannot display: `box` shows □ (U+25A1), and `hex` shows the character's code in hex digits. | [the glyph source issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/85) |
| `blink` | `--blink`, `--no-blink` | switch | on | on or off | vtium | top level, command line | Blink blinking text (SGR 5) and the cursor, every 500 ms. When off, neither blinks. | kmscon's `blink` key |
| `blink-text` | `--blink-text=VALUE` | one of `full`, `partial`, `off` | `partial` | the choices | vtium-render | top level, command line | How blinking text (SGR 5 or 6) looks while a blink is off. `full` hides it, `partial` dims it halfway to its background, as faint text (SGR 2) is, and `off` keeps it steady. The cursor follows `blink` either way. | [the blink options issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/81); the maintainer's decision of 2026-11-03 |
| `blink-decorations` | `--blink-decorations`, `--no-blink-decorations` | switch | off | on or off | vtium-render | top level, command line | Blink the underline and strikethrough of blinking text with it. They hide while a blink is off with `blink-text = full`, and dim with `partial`. When off, they stay visible while the text blinks. | [the blink options issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/81) |
| `allow-font-ops` | `--allow-font-ops`, `--no-allow-font-ops` | switch | on | on or off | vtium | top level, command line | Let programs switch the console's font, and ask which font is in use (xterm's OSC 50). A program switches with `OSC 50 ; NAME ST` and asks with `OSC 50 ; ? ST`. A switch lasts until that program's session ends; then vtium returns to the font and size that `font-name` and `font-size` set. `vtium-config use-frit NAME` switches the font with the same sequence. The query reports the name of the font on screen, or no name when that font has none a switch takes, such as a font file's path or a font family. When off, vtium ignores OSC 50, queries included. It is on by default, as xterm's `allowFontOps` is, because a program can choose only the installed font sets, the built-in fonts and the font its console started in, never another file. vtium reads a font set only when root owns it and no other user can change it or a folder above it. | [the issue that loads the configured font set](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/126) |
| `allow-window-ops` | `--allow-window-ops`, `--no-allow-window-ops` | switch | off | on or off | vtium | top level, command line | Let programs set the size of the console's text area in rows and columns (xterm's window operation `CSI 8 ; ROWS ; COLUMNS t`). vtium meets the request by changing the font size. It draws at the largest font size at which the displays hold that many rows and columns, and the console's grid becomes exactly that size. When the displays cannot hold the size even at the smallest font size, the grid gets as many rows and columns as they hold there. A number left out keeps that side as it is, and 0 fills the display on that side. The grid is exact, but a display may draw it in larger character cells than that font size gives, to fill more of the screen. A program that asks for the cell size, as with `CSI 16 t`, is told the cell of that font size. The size lasts until the session of the program that asked for it ends, or until you zoom. Then vtium returns to the size that `font-size` sets. When off, vtium ignores the request and changes nothing. It is off by default, as xterm's `allowWindowOps` is. A program can ask for the size in any case, with `CSI 18 t`. | [the font and window operations issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/44) |
| `text-direction` | `--text-direction=VALUE` | one of `ltr`, `rtl`, `auto` | `ltr` | the choices | vtium-term | top level, command line | Which way a paragraph of text runs when the program writing it does not say: `ltr`, left to right, `rtl`, right to left, or `auto`, which takes each paragraph's direction from its first letter. A paragraph is the text between two line ends. `ltr`, the default, starts each paragraph at the left edge, and `rtl` at the right edge. Under `auto`, a paragraph that starts with an Arabic or Hebrew letter runs right to left, and any other runs left to right. A paragraph keeps its direction however many rows it wraps across. `rtl` suits a console used mostly in Arabic, Hebrew or another right-to-left language. vtium reads this key when it starts, so a change takes effect when vtium restarts, and it never changes text already on the screen. A program can change the direction with escape sequences, and a terminal reset returns it to this setting. A build without right-to-left support (the `bidi` feature) accepts this key and does nothing with it. | [the right-to-left text issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/43) |

## Session and terminal

The command each console runs, the terminal type it sees, and how much of its output vtium keeps.

| Key | Option | Type | Default | Bound | Read by | Set in | What | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `login` | `--login -- COMMAND...`, `-l` | command | unset | 4095 bytes in a file | vtium | top level, `[head NAME]`, command line | The command each console runs, such as a login prompt or a shell. When unset, the command is `/bin/login -p` with `reset-env` on and `/bin/login` with it off. A word written `$NAME` is replaced by that environment variable's value, and `$$` writes a literal `$` at the start of a word. | kmscon's `login` key |
| `oneshot` | `--oneshot`, `--no-oneshot` | switch | off | on or off | vtium | top level, command line | Exit when the console's command exits, instead of starting it again. | kmscon's `oneshot` key |
| `term` | `--term=VALUE`, `-t` | text | `xterm-vtium` | 4095 bytes, no control character | vtium | top level, command line | The value of `TERM` that programs on the console see. The default is vtium's own terminfo entry, `xterm-vtium`, which is also named `vtium`. With either name, vtium answers capability queries (XTGETTCAP) from that entry. With `kmscon`, vtium answers from kmscon's entry. With any other value, vtium answers every query as unknown. | kmscon's `term` key |
| `reset-env` | `--reset-env`, `--no-reset-env` | switch | on | on or off | vtium | top level, command line | Start each console's command with only the environment variables vtium sets. When off, the command also gets vtium's own environment. | kmscon's `reset-env` key |
| `backspace-delete` | `--backspace-delete`, `--no-backspace-delete` | switch | on | on or off | vtium-platform | top level, command line | Backspace sends DEL (0x7f). When off, it sends BS (0x08). | kmscon's `backspace-delete` key |
| `sb-size` | `--sb-size=VALUE` | number (lines) | 1000 | 0 to 100000, clamped | vtium-term | top level, command line | How many lines of scrollback each console keeps, up to `sb-size-cap`. | kmscon's `sb-size` key |
| `sb-size-cap` | `--sb-size-cap=VALUE` | number (lines) | unset | 0 to 100000, clamped | vtium-term | top level, command line | The most lines `sb-size` can ask for. When unset, it depends on the machine's memory: 10,000 lines below 2 GiB, 30,000 from 2 GiB and 100,000 from 4 GiB. | [the configuration issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/21) |
| `sb-memory` | `--sb-memory=VALUE` | number (bytes) | 5242880 without image support, 4653056 with it | 1048576 to 1073741824, clamped | vtium-term | top level, command line | The most memory each console's scrollback uses. When it is full, the oldest lines are dropped, as they are past `sb-size`. The value is in bytes, or in KiB, MiB or GiB with `K`, `M` or `G` (such as `6M`), up to a quarter of the machine's memory (or up to the default when `/proc/meminfo` cannot be read). When unset, vtium sizes it to fit each console's size in characters, and sizes it again when that changes. A console up to 170x48 characters gets what is left of a 16 MiB budget after the console's screens and the rest of vtium, so a smaller console keeps more lines. A larger console gets the 170x48 value shown here. The default does not grow with the display or the machine's memory. On a machine with memory to spare, set `sb-memory` for a deeper scrollback; a set value stays fixed. | [the scrollback memory issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/131) |
| `bell` | `--bell`, `--no-bell` | switch | off | on or off | vtium | top level, command line | Ring the console's bell when a program sends BEL. A program can silence its own bells by resetting mode 1042, which starts set. When off, no bell rings. | kmscon's `bell` key |
| `sync-timeout` | `--sync-timeout=VALUE` | number (ms) | 200 | 0 to 10000, clamped | vtium | top level, command line | The longest vtium waits for a program to finish a synchronized update (mode 2026) before it shows the screen as it is. 0 turns mode 2026 off. | [the modes issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/12) |

## On-screen display and notices

What vtium shows on top of the console, and in which colors: which head and console you are looking at, a notice about a problem, and the kernel's warnings.

| Key | Option | Type | Default | Bound | Read by | Set in | What | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `osd` | `--osd=VALUE` | one of `off`, `minimal`, `full` | `minimal` | the choices | vtium | top level, command line | What the on-screen display shows at the top of each screen after a change, such as a console switch. `minimal` shows a dot in the top-right character cell: filled on the active head, hollow on the others. `full` shows a line across the top, such as `● desk · console 2 of 3`. `off` shows nothing. A notice about a problem appears whatever `osd` says. | [the on-screen display issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/169) |
| `osd-timeout` | `--osd-timeout=VALUE` | number (s), or `never` | 3 | 1 to 600, clamped, or `never` | vtium | top level, command line | How long the on-screen display stays visible after a change. `never` keeps it visible all the time. | [the on-screen display issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/169) |
| `focus-mark` | `--focus-mark=VALUE` | one of `auto`, `always`, `off` | unset | the choices | vtium | top level, command line | The old name for `osd` and `osd-timeout`. vtium reads it only when `osd` and `osd-timeout` are not set: `auto` means `osd = minimal`, `always` means `osd = minimal` with `osd-timeout = never`, and `off` means `osd = off`. When it is set, vtium logs the new keys. | [the on-screen display issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/169) |
| `kernel-messages` | `--kernel-messages=VALUE` | one of `after-plymouth`, `always` | `after-plymouth` | the choices | vtium | top level, command line | When vtium shows the kernel's warnings and errors on the screen. vtium shows each new kernel message whose level is warning or more severe, on top of the console, as long as the kernel's console log level lets it through. `quiet` and `loglevel=` on the kernel command line set that level. vtium never writes them into a console's session. `after-plymouth` leaves the messages to Plymouth, the boot splash program, while it runs, and vtium shows them once Plymouth has quit. Once Plymouth has quit, vtium does not go back and show the messages that came while it ran. On a machine without Plymouth, vtium shows them from its start. `always` shows them whether Plymouth runs or not. | [the boot messages issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/266) |
| `notice-foreground` | `--notice-foreground=VALUE` | color, `r,g,b` | `31,41,51` | each 0 to 255 | vtium | top level, command line | The text color of a notice. A notice is a box that reports a problem, such as errors in vtium.conf. It appears whatever `osd` says. | [the on-screen display issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/169) |
| `notice-background` | `--notice-background=VALUE` | color, `r,g,b` | `254,226,226` | each 0 to 255 | vtium | top level, command line | The background color of a notice. While a notice is showing, the on-screen display's line appears in the same box, in the notice's colors. | [the on-screen display issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/169) |
| `notice-border` | `--notice-border=VALUE` | color, `r,g,b` | `185,28,28` | each 0 to 255 | vtium | top level, command line | The border color of a notice. | [the on-screen display issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/169) |
| `osd-foreground` | `--osd-foreground=VALUE` | color, `r,g,b` | `229,231,235` | each 0 to 255 | vtium | top level, command line | The text color of the on-screen display: the line of `osd = full` and the dot of `osd = minimal`. | [the on-screen display issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/169) |
| `osd-background` | `--osd-background=VALUE` | color, `r,g,b` | `31,41,51` | each 0 to 255 | vtium | top level, command line | The background color of the on-screen display: behind the line of `osd = full`, and in the character cell behind the dot of `osd = minimal`. | [the on-screen display issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/169) |

## Displays

Each display's resolution, colors and density, how long vtium waits for a display when it starts, and how it draws to them.

| Key | Option | Type | Default | Bound | Read by | Set in | What | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `use-original-mode` | `--use-original-mode`, `--no-use-original-mode` | switch | off | on or off | vtium-platform | top level, command line | Keep each display's current resolution. When off, vtium sets each display's preferred resolution. | kmscon's `use-original-mode` key; [the native mode issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/5) |
| `mode` | `--mode=VALUE` | resolution, one per line | unset | names of 63 bytes, each side 1 to 65535 | vtium-platform | top level, command line | A display's resolution and refresh rate. `WxH[@RATE]` sets it for every display, `[CONNECTOR]WxH` for one connector, and `GPU[CONNECTOR]WxH` for one connector on one graphics card, named by its udev `ID_PATH`. Write one `mode` line per display; the most specific match wins. When unset, each display uses its preferred resolution. Setting it turns `use-original-mode` off. | kmscon's `mode` key |
| `display-depth` | `--display-depth=VALUE` | one of `auto`, `1`, `gray4`, `gray16`, `color` | `auto` | the choices | vtium-render | top level, `[look NAME]`, command line | How many colors or shades each display can show. `1` is black and white: each character cell is lit or dark by its colors, never by their brightness. `gray4` and `gray16` are for gray panels of 4 or 16 shades; vtium sends color and the panel converts it. `color` is full color. `auto` uses what the display reports. For `auto`, an fbdev device that reports 1 bit gets `1`, and a known DRM panel driver gives its levels. | [the 1-bit displays issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/135) |
| `display-dpi` | `--display-dpi=VALUE` | number (dpi) | unset | 20 to 1000, clamped | vtium | top level, `[look NAME]`, command line | The pixel density (DPI) used to turn `font-size` and a font set's `size=` from points into pixels, instead of the density each display reports. When unset, vtium measures each display's density from the physical size it reports. If a display reports none, vtium assumes 96 DPI and logs a warning once for that display. | [the issue that renders glyphs in the font helper](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/145) |
| `display-wait` | `--display-wait=VALUE` | number (s), or `forever` | 10 | 0 to 600, clamped, or `forever` | vtium | top level, command line | How long vtium waits for a display when it starts, counted from when its VT is shown. If no display appears in that time, vtium exits with status 1, so the unit's `OnFailure=` can start a getty. When vtium.conf's policy is closed, vtium waits as long as it takes, as with `forever`. vtium counts only while the VT is its own. If another program takes the VT before vtium's first frame is on screen, vtium waits for the VT to come back and then starts the full wait again. X does this at boot when it starts on another VT. With 0, vtium does not wait: only a display that is ready when the VT is shown counts. `forever` waits as long as it takes. `forever` suits a machine whose only display is a USB adapter (DisplayLink, `udl`) that may be plugged in at any time. Once a display has appeared, vtium never exits for lack of one. | [the configuration issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/21); [the issue about X starting during vtium's first frame](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/270) |
| `display-buffers` | `--display-buffers=VALUE` | one of `1`, `2`, `3` | unset | the choices | vtium-platform | top level, command line | How many frame buffers each display keeps (DRM displays only; every display gets the same number). `3` is triple buffering: no frame waits for the previous one to reach the screen, and each display needs one more frame of memory. `2` is double buffering. `1` is single buffering, which uses the least memory, but vtium then draws into the buffer on screen, so a half-drawn frame can show. A framebuffer device (fbdev) always keeps one buffer. When unset, the build decides: the number it was built with (`VTIUM_DISPLAY_BUFFERS`), or else 3 in a build with optional features, 2 in the smallest build (minspec), and 1 only in a build smaller than that. `vtium config get display-buffers` prints the draft's value followed by `draft`, or the build's default followed by `default` (`unset` when the build sets no number, in which case the rule above decides). | [the displays issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/18) |
| `hwaccel` | `--hwaccel`, `--no-hwaccel` | switch | off | on or off | vtium | top level, command line | Draw with the GPU, in a build that supports it. It is off unless vtium was built with it on (`VTIUM_HWACCEL`). `vtium config get hwaccel` prints the draft's value followed by `draft`, or the build's default followed by `default`. `vtium config set hwaccel on` turns it on in the draft. | kmscon's `hwaccel` key |
| `render-timer` | `--render-timer=VALUE` | one of `none`, `osd`, `log`, `both` | `none` | the choices | vtium-render | top level, command line | Measure each display's frame times once a second, and write the figures to the log, show them on screen, or both. | [the CPU compositor issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/16) |

## Power and blanking

When the displays turn off, and the keys that reboot, power off or suspend the machine.

| Key | Option | Type | Default | Bound | Read by | Set in | What | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dpms-timeout` | `--dpms-timeout=VALUE` | number (s) | 600 | 0 to 4294967295, clamped | vtium-platform | top level, command line | Turn the displays off after this long with no key press or mouse action (a move, a click or the wheel). 0 never turns them off. | kmscon's `dpms-timeout` key |
| `program-blank` | `--program-blank`, `--no-program-blank` | switch | on | on or off | vtium | top level, command line | Let a program set the blanking timeout and wake the displays, as `setterm --blank` does on the Linux console. A program sets the timeout with `CSI 9 ; n ]` (n minutes, up to 60; 0 never blanks) and wakes the displays with `CSI 13 ]`. A terminal reset (RIS) returns the timeout to `dpms-timeout`. When off, vtium ignores these sequences. A key press or mouse action wakes the displays either way. | [the screen blanking issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/79) |
| `key-reboot` | `--key-reboot=VALUE` | key combinations, `<Mod>...key`, separated by commas | unset | 4095 bytes; modifiers Shift, Lock, Control, Alt, Logo; keys as xkb names them | vtium | top level, command line | The key that reboots the machine. When unset, no key reboots. When `/proc/sys/kernel/ctrl-alt-del` is 0, vtium asks init to reboot, as Ctrl+Alt+Del does, so the services stop first; otherwise the kernel restarts at once. | the `grab-reboot` key that kmscon had |
| `key-power-off` | `--key-power-off=VALUE` | key combinations, `<Mod>...key`, separated by commas | unset | 4095 bytes; modifiers Shift, Lock, Control, Alt, Logo; keys as xkb names them | vtium | top level, command line | The key that powers the machine off. When unset, no key powers off. vtium asks init with `SIGRTMIN+4`, which systemd treats as `poweroff.target`, so the services stop and the filesystems are unmounted first. | [the configuration issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/21) |
| `key-suspend` | `--key-suspend=VALUE` | key combinations, `<Mod>...key`, separated by commas | unset | 4095 bytes; modifiers Shift, Lock, Control, Alt, Logo; keys as xkb names them | vtium | top level, command line | The key that suspends the machine to RAM. vtium asks logind to suspend. When logind is not running, or vtium was built without `logind`, vtium writes `mem` to `/sys/power/state`. When unset, no key suspends. Because vtium asks logind, anything that holds off sleep through logind can still do so. | [the configuration issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/21) |

## Images

Sixel and kitty graphics, how much memory images use, which protocols vtium offers, and the helper that reads and decodes them.

| Key | Option | Type | Default | Bound | Read by | Set in | What | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `image-storage-limit` | `--image-storage-limit=VALUE` | number (bytes), or `auto` | `auto` | 0 to 1099511627776, clamped, or `auto` | vtium-image | top level, command line | The most memory each console uses for images, on both its screens together. The value is in bytes, or in KiB, MiB or GiB with `K`, `M` or `G` (such as `64M`), up to 1 TiB. `auto` gives each console enough for four screenfuls of its head's displays, from 16 MiB to 192 MiB. `0` turns sixel and kitty graphics off. `auto` recalculates when a display is added, removed or resized. A build without image support accepts this key and shows no images. | [the image pipeline issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/28); Ghostty's `image-storage-limit` |
| `sixel` | `--sixel`, `--no-sixel` | switch | on | on or off | vtium-term | top level, command line | Show sixel images. When off, vtium neither offers nor shows sixel: its device attributes (DA1) leave out attribute 4, and it ignores sixel data. vtium offers sixel only while `image-storage-limit` is above 0 and every display of the console's head can show images. A build without image support never offers it. | [the sixel issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/48) |
| `kitty-graphics` | `--kitty-graphics`, `--no-kitty-graphics` | switch | on | on or off | vtium-term | top level, command line | Show images sent with the kitty graphics protocol. When off, vtium neither offers nor shows them: it ignores graphics commands and does not answer queries. vtium offers it only while `image-storage-limit` is above 0 and every display of the console's head can show images. A build without image support never offers it. | [the kitty graphics issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/49) |
| `max-graphic-size` | `--max-graphic-size=VALUE` | size, `WxH` | `10000x10000` | each side 1 to 65535 | vtium-image | top level, command line | The largest image a program can send, in pixels (`WxH`), for sixel and kitty graphics alike. vtium refuses a larger one. A build without image support accepts this key and shows no images. | [the image pipeline issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/28); xterm's `maxGraphicSize` |
| `num-color-registers` | `--num-color-registers=VALUE` | number (registers) | 1024 | 2 to 65535, clamped | vtium-term | top level, command line | How many colors a sixel image can use (its color registers), and the most a program can ask for with XTSMGRAPHICS. A build without image support accepts this key and shows no images. | [the image pipeline issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/28); xterm's `numColorRegisters` |
| `private-color-registers` | `--private-color-registers`, `--no-private-color-registers` | switch | on | on or off | vtium-term | top level, command line | Give each sixel image its own colors (mode 1070, after a reset). When on, each sixel image starts from the default colors. When off, images share their colors. A build without image support accepts this key and shows no images. | [the image pipeline issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/28); xterm's `privateColorRegisters` |
| `image-helper` | `--image-helper=VALUE` | text | `/usr/bin/vtium-image` | 4095 bytes, no control character | vtium | top level, command line | The image helper: the program vtium starts, as the logged-in user, to read image files and shared memory for kitty graphics and to decode PNG and zlib-compressed images. vtium runs as root and does neither itself. vtium opens the program once, when it starts, and runs every helper from that file, so a newly installed helper takes effect when vtium restarts. vtium refuses a helper whose path is not absolute, that is not a regular file, that is setuid or setgid, that anyone but root or vtium's own account owns, or that its group or other users can write. It then logs why and refuses images: `EBADF` for files and shared memory, `EINVAL` for PNG and zlib. vtium starts the helper through `/proc/self/fd`, so `/proc` must be mounted. A build without image support accepts this key and starts no helper. The default is the path vtium was built with. | [the image helper issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/31); the maintainer's decision of 2026-11-01 |

## Running vtium

Where vtium finds its configuration, its log, the font helper that draws a font's characters, and the character cache.

| Key | Option | Type | Default | Bound | Read by | Set in | What | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `configdir` | `--configdir=VALUE`, `-c` | text | `/etc/vtium` | 4095 bytes, no control character | vtium | command line | The directory that holds `vtium.conf`, vtium's configuration file. | kmscon's `configdir` key |
| `help` | `--help`, `-h` | switch | off | on or off | vtium | command line | Print the options and exit. | kmscon's `help` key |
| `version` | `--version`, `-V` | switch | off | on or off | vtium | command line | Print the version, the source revision of the build, and the optional features it was built with, then exit. | kmscon's `version` key |
| `debug` | `--debug`, `--no-debug` | switch | off | on or off | vtium | top level, command line | Log debug messages too, to help find what went wrong. When off, vtium logs information messages, warnings and errors. | kmscon's `debug` key |
| `font-helper` | `--font-helper=VALUE` | text | `/usr/bin/vtium-config` | 4095 bytes, no control character | vtium | top level, command line | The font helper: the program vtium starts to draw a font set's characters. It runs as `nobody` when vtium runs as root. vtium opens the program once, when it starts, and runs every helper from that file, so a newly installed helper takes effect when vtium restarts. vtium refuses a helper whose path is not absolute, that is not a regular file, that is setuid or setgid, that anyone but root or vtium's own account owns, or that its group or other users can write. It then logs why and uses its built-in font. vtium starts the helper through `/proc/self/fd`, so `/proc` must be mounted. The default is the path vtium was built with. | [the issue that renders glyphs in the font helper](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/145); the maintainer's decision of 2026-11-01 |
| `glyph-cache` | `--glyph-cache=VALUE` | one of `minspec`, `performance` | unset | the choices | vtium-render | top level, command line | How much memory vtium uses to cache drawn characters. When unset, `minspec` (small), or `performance` in a build with the `performance-cache` feature. | [the CPU compositor issue](https://github.com/vtium/vtium/issues/16) |

## Other color schemes for the notices and the on-screen display

`install/vtium.conf.example` carries these schemes for the six color keys, commented out, for color blindness and personal preference. vtium draws whatever colors are set and checks no contrast between a text and its box.

| Scheme | What it is | `notice-foreground` | `notice-background` | `notice-border` | `osd-foreground` | `osd-background` | `osd-border` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `light` | For a light terminal background: the on-screen display is a pale grey box with dark text and a grey edge, and a notice a dark red box with white text and a darker edge, so a problem differs from a status in brightness as well as in hue. | `255,255,255` | `153,27,27` | `69,10,10` | `31,41,51` | `243,244,246` | `156,163,175` |
| `dark` | Both boxes are dark, for a dark terminal background: a notice is deep red with pale text and a light red edge, and the on-screen display near black with light grey text and a grey edge. | `254,226,226` | `185,28,28` | `248,113,113` | `209,213,219` | `17,24,39` | `75,85,99` |
| `color-blind-safe` | For color blindness, a problem differs from a status in brightness and in an orange and blue pair, never in red against green: a notice is a bright orange box with near-black text, and the on-screen display a dark blue box with near-white text. | `28,25,23` | `255,176,0` | `254,97,0` | `238,242,255` | `11,42,91` | `100,143,255` |
